messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw an ~8% p99 tail regression in the canary after the kernel-selection patch landed. Symptoms look host-side (parse/tokenize/stream handoff) not GPU.
ben: Which canary? any flamegraphs or traces?
maria: canary-3390012345. I ran a quick sampler and attached the hot stacks below. Biggest delta is in the ingress parse path: proto-unpack -> tokenize -> writev. CPU time on host up ~25% for that path.
alex: gist of the stack (sampler):\n```\n  35%  runtime_proxy  proxy_ingress_parse
  20%  runtime_proxy  tokenize_payload
  15%  runtime_proxy  writev_coalesce
  10%  libc.so       memcpy
  05%  runtime_proxy  kvcache_lookup
```
ciara: Interesting — kvcache_lookup shows up but only 5%. Did you check kvcache hit/miss rates around the regression window?
maria: yes — kvcache hit ratio dropped from 0.78 -> 0.61 on this canary run. Evictions spiked. Raw numbers:\n```\n  kvcache.hits: 780k -> 610k
  kvcache.requests: 1.0m -> 1.0m
  kvcache.evictions/sec: 90 -> 420
```
ben: That eviction blowup could cause extra proto-unpack pressure if we start re-decoding prefixes more often. Also saw more small writes which hurts net syscalls.
alex: I think two things are interacting: kernel-selector changed batching boundaries slightly (smaller minibatches for certain seq-len distributions) -> more streaming fragments -> more tokenization calls and more writev syscalls.
ciara: Do we have metrics on avg fragment size / writes per request before/after?
maria: yes: avg-fragment-size dropped 1.2k -> 720 bytes, writes-per-request increased 1.8x. HTTP2 windowing + our chunker ends up producing more microframes.
ben: Quick hypothesis: newer kernel selection prefers low-latency kernels that assume larger continuous input. When we fragment earlier, we lose prefix cache locality and increase host-side overhead.
alex: Repro locally with the replay harness: `./tools/replay --trace=ingress --canary=3390012345 --capture=host`. On my laptop you can toggle `--kernel-hint=old` to compare.
maria: Short mitigation options: (a) revert kernel selector change in canary, (b) patch chunker to merge small fragments up to 1k before handing off to tokenizer, (c) increase kvcache capacity on canary nodes to validate if eviction is root cause.
ciara: (b) looks low-risk and quick to test. I can put a small coalescer in the sidecar that waits up to 200us or until 1k bytes.
ben: I'll prototype the coalescer and run the replay. If it drops writes-per-request and restores kvcache hit rate, we know it's fragmentation-induced.
alex: Plan: ciara lands coalescer in a canary flip tomorrow morning (10:00 PT), ben runs replay and collection (flamegraph + kvcache metrics), maria will correlate p99 and evictions. If that fixes, follow-up is kernel-selector tweak or permanent coalescer + unit tests.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-3390012345: rollback triggered (user: alex) — reason: p99 regression observed. :warning:
alex: Thanks — keep notes in the PR. I'll open a tracking issue and tag perf/ingress.
maria: Adding perf counters to the canary so we can graph fragment-size distribution over time.
ben: sharing quick test command: `./tools/replay --replay=/captures/3390012345 --enable-coalesce --num-iter=500 --out=perf.tar`
ciara: will run after lunch and post results here. :coffee:
alex: awesome. if coalescer doesn't help we revert kernel-selector for now and do a deeper kvcache/backpressure audit."
